name: Sotorasib
mechanism: Covalently binds cysteine 12 of KRAS G12C within the switch-II pocket, locking KRAS in its inactive GDP-bound state and suppressing MAPK signalling.
keyToxicities: Hepatotoxicity (transaminase elevation), with higher risk when started soon after immune checkpoint inhibitors
monitoring: Liver function tests before and regularly during early treatment
interactions: Avoid acid-reducing agents (or separate timing per label). Avoid strong CYP3A4 inducers. Sotorasib is a CYP3A4 inducer and may reduce exposure of sensitive substrates; it may increase exposure of P-gp substrates.
resistance: Secondary KRAS mutations (e.g. Y96D, R68S, H95X), KRAS G12C amplification, bypass activation (MET amplification, NRAS/BRAF mutations, RTK fusions), adaptive RTK/SHP2 feedback and histological transformation.
